mainTopic: How עדים זוממין pay: רב's rule that a single witness pays his share, and how the court values false testimony about a כתובה or a loan's due date
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: רב נחמן's statement is read as agreeing with רבה, not as a separate reason. Then רב teaches that an עד זומם pays 'according to his share.' The גמרא tries several cases to explain this. It rejects each one in turn, until it settles on a witness who admits that a בית דין already found them to be זוממין and ordered them to pay money. In that case, even רבי עקיבא agrees he pays his share based on his own admission, even though his admission cannot obligate his partner. Next comes a משנה about false witnesses who said a man divorced his wife without paying her כתובה. They pay only the market value of the uncertain right to collect it. רב חסדא, רב נתן בר אושעיא and רב פפא disagree about whose side the court prices. A second משנה deals with witnesses who said a loan was due in thirty days when the borrower says ten years. They pay the value of the extra time. The גמרא then brings שמואל's rule that a ten-year loan is still cancelled by שביעית, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Isn't רב נחמן's statement the same as רבה's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב נחמן's statement really means. If it means the witnesses 'did not perform an action', that is exactly רבה's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רב נחמן's statement mean? That the witnesses did not do an action? But that is just רבה's reasoning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going back to a statement it quoted just before this, from רב נחמן. It points out that this statement seems to add nothing beyond what רבה already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא expects every quoted opinion to add something new. If רב נחמן's point is only that the witnesses 'did not do an action', then he is repeating רבה's reason, and listing his statement as a second explanation makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it mean?
They did not perform an action; their testimony did not actually cause any loss to happen

phrases.english: What is it? That they did not perform an action?
phrases.notes: This asks what רב נחמן meant when he said the money stays with its owner.

phrases.english: That is the same as רבה's reasoning!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נִיהוּ, דְּלֹא עָשׂוּ מַעֲשֶׂה? הַיְינוּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבה and רב נחמן, which is not part of this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: Presenting רב נחמן's statement as a separate explanation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two explanations have the same content, רב נחמן's statement is repetitive.

steps.title: Read it as 'and likewise said רב נחמן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes how רב נחמן's statement is introduced. It is not a different opinion; it is a statement agreeing with רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'And so too said רב נחמן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by adjusting the wording. רב נחמן is agreeing with רבה, not offering a new reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רב נחמן's statement looked like a second, separate explanation. Once the introduction becomes 'וכן אמר', it is clear that he is supporting רבה's view in his own words. The problem of repetition goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; a signal that the wording should be read differently
And likewise said; a sign of agreement, not of disagreement

phrases.english: Say: 'And likewise said רב נחמן.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing how the statement is introduced, so it reads as agreeing with רבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן was giving a separate explanation that adds nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן simply agrees with רבה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן and רבה hold the same view. רב נחמן's words are a statement of agreement, not a new reason.

steps.title: רב: a conspiring witness pays according to his share
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב, who says that an עד זומם pays only his own share.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A conspiring witness pays according to his share.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins here. It is a short rule from רב about how an עד זומם pays money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is short and unclear: what is 'his share'? The next steps of the גמרא try to work out exactly which case רב is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness proven false by other witnesses who say, 'You were with us somewhere else at that time'
According to his share; only his own portion

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
A conspiring witness pays according to his share.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: עֵד זוֹמֵם מְשַׁלֵּם לְפִי חֶלְקוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the earlier discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עד זומם pays only his own share.

steps.title: What does 'according to his share' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רב means by 'pays according to his share.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'pays according to his share' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב's words mean. This is a setup line; next the גמרא will try out possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for an explanation, not an attack. The phrase could fit more than one case, so the גמרא must decide which one רב means.

phrases.english: What does 'pays according to his share' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְשַׁלֵּם לְפִי חֶלְקוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רב's rule in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case רב's rule is talking about

steps.title: Each pays half? A משנה already teaches that
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is that each of the two witnesses pays half. The גמרא rejects it because a משנה already teaches that money is divided between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that this witness pays half and that witness pays half, we already learned in a משנה: money is divided among them, but lashes are not divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first explanation: two false witnesses split the payment. It then rejects it, because רב would not need to teach something a משנה already says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה already teaches that payment of money is divided among the witnesses, while each one gets the full lashes. If רב only meant that each pays half, his teaching would be repetitive. So רב must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
They divide (the punishment among the witnesses)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא disagrees with the idea that each witness pays half. That idea is true. It is rejected only as an explanation of רב, because רב would be repeating the משנה.

phrases.english: If you say that this one pays half
and that one pays half,
we already learned: they divide money,
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later in this מסכת, on דף ה.

phrases.english: but they do not divide lashes!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּהַאי מְשַׁלֵּם פַּלְגָא וְהַאי מְשַׁלֵּם פַּלְגָא, תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to the question of step 4 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining רב as 'each witness pays half'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule is already taught in a משנה, so רב's statement would be repetitive.

steps.title: Only one witness was proven false and he pays his half
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: only one of the two witnesses was proven false, and he pays his own half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a case where only one of them was proven false, and he pays his own half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new explanation of רב. Only one witness was caught as an עד זומם, and he pays his half alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would make רב's teaching new: even when only one witness is proven false, he still pays his portion. It is no longer just a repeat of the משנה, which talks about both witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Was proven false as an עד זומם

phrases.english: Rather: for example, where one of them was proven false,
that he pays his own half.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כְּגוֹן דְּאִיתַּזּוּם חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restricting the rule to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was talking about both witnesses splitting the payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was talking about a case where only one witness was proven false.

steps.title: No payment unless both are proven false
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second explanation with a ברייתא: an עד זומם pays money only when both witnesses are proven false.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he pay at all? But a ברייתא teaches: a conspiring witness does not pay money until both of them are proven false!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation from step 6. A ברייתא says that when only one witness is proven false, he pays nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The penalty of הזמה applies only to a full set of witnesses. If only one is proven false, there is no הזמה payment at all. So רב cannot mean that one witness pays his half in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: But does he? Introduces a challenge
But isn't it so that; introduces a contradicting source
That both of them are proven false as עדים זוממין

phrases.english: And does he pay?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תַּנְיָא: אֵין עֵד זוֹמֵם מְשַׁלֵּם מָמוֹן
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: a conspiring witness does not pay money
until both of them are proven false!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מְשַׁלֵּם? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining רב as a case where only one witness was proven false
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that no money is paid unless both witnesses are proven false.

steps.title: רבא: the witness admits 'I testified falsely'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רב is talking about a witness who admits on his own that he testified falsely, so he pays his share.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is talking about a witness who says, 'I gave false testimony.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation of רב that avoids the ברייתא. The case is not about הזמה through other witnesses at all. It is about a witness who confesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only rules about הזמה, where other witnesses prove the pair false. רבא moves רב's rule to a case of confession, where the witness pays his share because of his own admission. That way רב's rule does not conflict with the ברייתא.

phrases.english: רבא said:
It is talking about one who says, 'I gave false testimony.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּאוֹמֵר עֵדוּת שֶׁקֶר הֵעַדְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by moving the rule to a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the rule to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was talking about real הזמה of one witness.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was talking about a witness who confesses that he lied.

steps.title: Once a witness has testified, he cannot take it back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: does a witness have the power to cancel his testimony? Once he has testified, he cannot change it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it in his power? Once he has testified, he cannot go back and testify differently!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's explanation. Under a basic rule of testimony, a witness's later confession that he lied counts for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule: כיון שהגיד שוב אינו חוזר ומגיד. Once a witness has given testimony, a later change of story is not accepted. So how can his confession make him pay anything?

keyTerms.meaning: Is it in his power? Can he decide this on his own?

keyTerms.term: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיד שׁוּב אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּמַגִּיד
keyTerms.meaning: Once he has testified, he cannot go back and testify differently

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that a witness cannot take back his testimony, is a basic rule of testimony throughout ש״ס. Because of it, רבא's explanation is dropped, and the next step (אלא) gives a new case.

phrases.english: Is it in his power?
phrases.notes: Literally 'is it all like him?' It means: can his word alone change the testimony?

phrases.english: Once he has testified,
he cannot go back and testify again!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל כְּמִינֵּיהּ? כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיד שׁוּב אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּמַגִּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's explanation from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the witness admitted he lied
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A witness cannot take back his testimony after giving it, so his confession should have no legal effect.

steps.title: The witness admits a court already found them to be false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב's case is a witness who says: we testified and were found to be עדים זוממין in a certain court.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב is talking about a witness who says: 'We testified and were proven to be false witnesses in such-and-such a court.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of רב's ruling after the last one was rejected in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said a witness cannot take back his own testimony. So here the witness is not taking anything back. He is admitting that a בית דין already found him to be a זומם, and that admission makes him pay his share.

keyTerms.meaning: We were proven to be עֵדִים זוֹמְמִין

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case of one who says:
"We testified and were proven false witnesses
in such-and-such a court."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּאוֹמֵר הֵעַדְנוּ וְהוּזַמְנוּ בְּבֵית דִּין פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by changing the case from taking back testimony to admitting an earlier court ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's witness is cancelling his own testimony, which he cannot do.
steps.terutzMaskana: The witness is admitting that a בית דין already found them to be זוממין, so he pays his share based on his admission.

steps.title: This answer does not fit רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this follows. It cannot be רבי עקיבא, who holds that an עד זומם does not pay based on his own admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Not רבי עקיבא's. If it followed רבי עקיבא, he says a false witness also does not pay based on his own admission!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 10 by showing it clashes with רבי עקיבא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 makes the witness pay because of what he admits. But רבי עקיבא holds that an עד זומם never pays by his own admission. So step 10's answer would mean רב goes against רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: According to whom?
Not according to רבי עקיבא,
for if it were according to רבי עקיבא,
doesn't he say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ!
phrases.english: he also does not pay based on his own admission!
phrases.notes: "He" means an עד זומם. רבי עקיבא treats his payment like a fine, and a fine is not paid by admitting it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the witness pays because he admits they were found to be זוממין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא holds an עד זומם does not pay by his own admission, so the answer puts רב against רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The court had also ordered them to pay money
steps.stepSummary: רב's case is narrowed further: the witness admits they were found to be זוממין and were also ordered to pay money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the witness says: 'We testified and were proven to be false witnesses in such-and-such a court, and we were ordered to pay money.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the case once more so that it fits רבי עקיבא too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the בית דין already ordered a set amount, the witness is no longer admitting to a fine. He is admitting an ordinary money debt. Even רבי עקיבא agrees that a person pays an ordinary debt based on his own admission.

keyTerms.meaning: And we were ordered to pay money

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case of one who says
"We testified and were proven false witnesses
in such-and-such a court
and we were ordered to pay money."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּאוֹמֵר הֵעַדְנוּ וְהוּזַמְנוּ בְּבֵית דִּין פְּלוֹנִי וְחוּיַּיבְנוּ מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by adding that the court already ordered payment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witness admits to being a זומם, which by רבי עקיבא is like admitting to a fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the court already ordered payment, it is a regular debt, and everyone agrees one pays a debt based on his own admission.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's single עד זומם pays his share only when he admits that a בית דין found them to be זוממין and also ordered them to pay.

steps.title: What רב is teaching us
steps.stepSummary: One might think that since this witness cannot make his partner pay, he does not pay either. רב teaches that he does pay his share.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since he cannot make his fellow witness pay, he himself also does not pay. So רב teaches us that he does pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new idea in רב's ruling, closing this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One person's admission cannot obligate the other witness, because that needs two witnesses. One might think this means the admission is worth nothing even for himself. רב teaches that his admission still obligates him for his own share.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (what one might have thought)

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since his fellow witness
he cannot make liable,
he himself also is not liable,
so he teaches us that he is.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב needed to state the ruling set up in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A single witness's admission obligates him for his own share, even though it cannot obligate his partner.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an admission can obligate the person who admits even when it has no effect on anyone else.

steps.title: New משנה: false testimony about an unpaid כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: witnesses say a man divorced his wife and did not pay her כתובה. But sooner or later he will have to pay her כתובה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Witnesses say, 'We testify that so-and-so divorced his wife and did not give her the כתובה.' But isn't it true that whether today or tomorrow, in the end he will have to give her the כתובה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets up a problem: how much do עדים זוממין pay if they testified about a כתובה that the husband would have had to pay someday anyway?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses did not create a debt out of nothing, because the husband would owe the כתובה eventually anyway, at divorce or death. So they cannot simply be made to pay the full כתובה. The משנה is preparing to explain how their payment is worked out.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a husband owes his wife at divorce or his death
In the end he will have to give

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"We testify about so-and-so
that he divorced his wife
and did not give her the כתובה,"
but isn't it so that whether today or tomorrow,
in the end he will give her the כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעִידִין אָנוּ אֶת אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי שֶׁגֵּירַשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The discussion of רב's ruling is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין who testified about an unpaid כתובה cannot simply pay the full amount, since the husband would have to pay it eventually anyway.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the witnesses pay the whole כתובה. The point is that the debt would come due someday anyway, so their payment must be worked out differently.

steps.title: The witnesses pay the market value of the כתובה right
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the court estimates how much a buyer would pay for this woman's כתובה. The buyer would collect if she is widowed or divorced, but would get nothing if she dies first, because her husband inherits her.
steps.simpleTranslation: We estimate how much a person would be willing to pay for this woman's כתובה. If she becomes a widow or is divorced, the buyer collects. But if she dies first, her husband inherits her and the buyer gets nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from step 14 gives its ruling: the עדים זוממין pay the value of the כתובה as a risky, uncertain right, not its full amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband would really owe the כתובה only later, and maybe never, because if his wife dies first he owes nothing. So the witnesses tried to cause him a loss equal only to that uncertain right. The court measures it by asking what a buyer would pay for the chance to collect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule the whole גמרא will now explain: the punishment of עדים זוממין follows the real value of the harm they tried to cause.

phrases.english: We estimate how much a person would want
to give for the כתובה of this woman,
phrases.notes: He means buying her right to collect the כתובה in the future.

phrases.english: since if she is widowed or divorced,
phrases.notes: The words 'the buyer collects' are left out here, but that is what's meant.

phrases.english: but if she dies,
her husband will inherit her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמְדִין כַּמָּה אָדָם רוֹצֶה לִיתֵּן בִּכְתוּבָּתָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in step 14 by giving its ruling on how much the witnesses pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses pay the market value of the uncertain right to collect this woman's כתובה, taking into account that if she dies first the husband inherits and nothing is collected.

steps.title: How exactly is the value assessed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking how the court actually makes this estimate.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How do we make the estimate?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a practical question about the משנה: how is this value measured? This sets up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said to estimate what a buyer would pay, but it did not say whose right is being priced. The גמרא wants to know the exact method.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
How do we assess it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד שָׁמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical method behind the משנה's ruling in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose right to the כתובה is being priced, and how is that value worked out?

steps.title: רב חסדא: measure from the husband's side
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the estimate is made in terms of the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We assess it from the husband's side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the first answer: the value is measured from the husband's point of view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court looks at the husband's chance of never paying, because his wife may die first and he would inherit her. The court asks how much someone would pay for that chance of the husband.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
In terms of the husband.
phrases.notes: He means pricing the husband's chance that she dies first, so he never has to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא בַּבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The value is measured from the husband's side, based on his chance of inheriting her and never paying.

steps.title: רב נתן בר אושעיא: measure from the wife's side
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אושעיא answers that the estimate is made in terms of the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אושעיא says: We assess it from the wife's side.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer: the value is measured from the wife's point of view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the court prices the wife's chance of collecting, meaning the chance that her husband dies first or divorces her. This is the other side of the same uncertainty that רב חסדא looked at.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions price the same uncertain כתובה. The difference is only which side's chance is being priced: the husband's chance of not paying, or the wife's chance of collecting.

phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Oshaya says:
In terms of the wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא אוֹמֵר בָּאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 16, disagreeing with רב חסדא in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The value is measured from the wife's side, based on her chance of collecting the כתובה.

steps.title: רב פפא: the wife's side, and only her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the estimate is made in terms of the wife, and only in terms of her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We assess it from the wife's side, and only for her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא agrees with רב נתן בר אושעיא that the wife's side is used, but adds a limit: only her כתובה is counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and her כתובה' narrow the calculation. Other money connected to the marriage is not counted, such as the husband's right to the profits from property she brought in. Only the value of the כתובה right is priced.

keyTerms.meaning: And in terms of her כתובה (only)
The wife's own property, whose profits go to the husband

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה prices the כתובה as an uncertain right. רב חסדא measures it from the husband's side, רב נתן בר אושעיא from the wife's side, and רב פפא from the wife's side counting only her כתובה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In terms of the wife, and in terms of her כתובה.
phrases.notes: He means only the כתובה is counted, not other marriage-related money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא בָּאִשָּׁה וּבִכְתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב נתן בר אושעיא's view in step 18 and adds a limit to what is counted.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The value is measured from the wife's side, counting only her כתובה and not other related rights.

steps.title: New case: the witnesses say thirty days, the borrower says ten years
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a case where witnesses claim a loan is due in thirty days, while the borrower says it is due in ten years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Witnesses say: "We testify that this man owes his friend 1,000 זוז, and he must pay it back within thirty days." The borrower says: "No, I have ten years to pay it back."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It describes the case first, and the ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the debt is real. The only argument is about the due date. If the witnesses turn out to be false, the damage they tried to cause is not the 1,000 זוז. It is the loss of having to pay back early.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the argument is over whether he owes the money. Everyone agrees he owes 1,000 זוז. The only question is when he has to pay.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"We testify about so-and-so
that he owes his fellow a thousand zuz,
on condition that he give them to him
from now until thirty days,"
and he says,
phrases.notes: "He" is the borrower, giving his own version of the loan.

phrases.english: "from now until ten years."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מְעִידִין אָנוּ בְּאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב לַחֲבֵירוֹ אֶלֶף זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a case parallel to the כתובה case in step 15, where the damage also has to be estimated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the witnesses say the loan is due in thirty days, and the borrower says ten years.

steps.title: The court estimates the value of the extra time
steps.stepSummary: The court figures out how much a person would pay to hold 1,000 זוז for ten years instead of thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court estimates how much a person would pay to have 1,000 זוז in hand. They compare paying it back in thirty days with paying it back in ten years. The difference is the amount the witnesses must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its ruling. The court puts a price on the extra time the false witnesses tried to take away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding money for ten years is worth much more than holding it for thirty days. The witnesses tried to take that advantage away from the borrower. So they pay the value of that difference, not the whole 1,000 זוז.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it will be in his hand, meaning he gets to use the money

steps.whatToRemember: Just like the כתובה case, the false witnesses pay only the real value of the damage they tried to cause. Here that damage is losing the extra time to repay.

phrases.english: We estimate how much a person would want to give
so that a thousand zuz would be in his hand,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין נוֹתְנָן מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: between giving them back from now until thirty days,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין נוֹתְנָן מִכָּאן וְעַד עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: and giving them back from now until ten years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמְדִים כַּמָּה אָדָם רוֹצֶה לִיתֵּן וְיִהְיוּ בְּיָדוֹ אֶלֶף זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case described in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses pay the difference in value between holding 1,000 זוז for ten years and holding it for thirty days.

steps.title: שמואל: a ten-year loan is still cancelled by שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if someone lends money for ten years, the seventh year cancels the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if someone lends his friend money for ten years, שביעית cancels the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a rule from שמואל about long-term loans and שביעית. This sets up the discussion that follows about the משנה's ten-year loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ten-year loan will surely pass through a שביעית year. One might have thought a loan that is not yet due is safe from שביעית. שמואל says it is still cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year of the cycle, שמיטה

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the משנה's ten-year loan to the laws of שמיטת כספים.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One who lends to his fellow for ten years,
the seventh year cancels it.
phrases.notes: This is the release of debts in the שמיטה year, דברים 15:1–2.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לְעֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה by bringing a rule about long-term loans and שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan made for ten years is cancelled by שביעית, even though it was not yet due.
